Looping Priyom in to triage. Notes / hypothesis before you dig in: 
- Customer reports 502s only when traffic goes through their proxy. That suggests header/transfer encoding or timeout behavior at the proxy could be converting transient 401s or connection resets into 502s.
- They bundle tool-calling + embeddings in a single request (larger payload + longer server processing).

Triage checklist (Priyom):
1) Use the attached redwood_sdk_snippet.py to reproduce talking to our hosted endpoint and to a small Redwood staging endpoint that accepts the same model. Run with/without streaming enabled.

3) Capture full request/response headers and any upstream logs that mention connection resets, header errors, or chunked-encoding issues.
4) Test with SDK option toggles: streaming on/off, use_chunked true/false, and different timeouts (30s, 45s, 60s).

Please capture concrete curl commands and the minimal repro that Tom can run. Keep this thread — the customer is sensitive to timing.

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Post-demo: Acme Health SDK auth & routing recap

I ran a quick repro matrix this morning using the snippet (attached) and an nginx proxy configured to rewrite Connection and remove Transfer-Encoding headers (to mimic the Kong plugin they described). Findings: 

What I reproduced:
- 502 returned consistently when the proxy stripped Transfer-Encoding: chunked and also removed Connection headers on requests larger than ~12KB.
- Direct calls (no proxy) and calls through a proxy that preserves Transfer-Encoding worked fine.
- When streaming is enabled in the SDK we send chunked body; if the proxy removes that header the server closes the connection which leads to a 502 at the gateway.

Quick technical notes & recommended temporary mitigations:
- Root cause: proxy is altering HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer semantics; the backend expects chunked bodies for streaming/large payloads. Proxy returns 502 upstream when it gets a truncated/altered stream.
- Short-term customer workarounds: 
  * Set SDK option use_chunked=false and disable streaming (falls back to single POST with full body) OR
  * Configure proxy to preserve Transfer-Encoding and Connection headers (preferred) and increase proxy read timeout to 90s.
- SDK change we can ship: add header-sanitization detection and a fallback to non-chunked mode when we detect intermediate proxies stripping chunked semantics. I can prototype a patch and push to a feature branch; ETA for PR: 2027-04-22.

Repro commands I used (minimal):
1) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @payload.json https://staging-infer.redwood.com/v1/generate
2) Run same curl through local nginx with config: proxy_set_header Connection ""; proxy_set_header Transfer-Encoding ""; (to simulate their Kong).

Logs excerpt: 
- upstream response: "502 Bad Gateway - connection reset by peer while reading response header from upstream"
- server error: "client prematurely closed connection"

I'll prepare a short internal playbook (1-pager) that Marissa can share with Acme infra: what to change in proxy config and quick SDK toggles.

-- Priyom

Tom / Lina — quick summary and proposed mutual action plan after internal triage: 

What we found:
- Root cause likely an edge proxy (Kong plugin) stripping Transfer-Encoding/Connection headers when requests are chunked, which converts streaming/large-payload flows into truncated upstreams and manifests as 502s.

Short-term actions (this week):
1) Acme infra: temporarily set SDK to non-chunked mode (use_chunked=false) and disable streaming for the problematic route. Test for 24 hours and report error rate. (Owner: Acme infra)
2) Acme infra: if comfortable, update Kong to preserve Transfer-Encoding and set proxy read timeout to 90s (Owner: Acme infra).
3) Redwood: Priyom will push a feature-branch patch that auto-detects header stripping and falls back to non-chunked mode; PR ETA: 2027-04-22. (Owner: Redwood Eng)
4) Redwood: Marissa will draft a 1-page proxy checklist and the quick MAP doc and share the Drive link. (Owner: Marissa)
